mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 anticipates a Fed rate cut within the next 20 days, causing a positive forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 20-day windows where the trigger occurs, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat (median <= 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PAYEMS (employment growth) of more than 50,000 jobs in a single month coincides with increased consumer confidence and corporate hiring forecasts, driving a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a single month
failure_condition: Across 10 such triggered months, the average 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 5 points over two months indicates weakening manufacturing momentum, which suppresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Over 20 such 60-day windows, the average negative return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls by more than 0.2 percentage points in three consecutive months, the S&P 500 expects a sustained economic recovery and delivers a positive 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2pp over 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 5 such episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not positively skewed (median <= 0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST (housing starts) above their 12-month averages for two months creates a dual-demand signal that drives a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month avg AND HOUST > 12-month avg for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During 10 such interaction-activated windows, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in RSAFS (money supply growth) below -2% for four consecutive months suggests a deflationary bias, which typically precedes a Fed hold or cut and supports a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >2% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 8 such triggered windows, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS falls by 20,000 jobs in a month followed by two months of unemployment rate above 4%, the S&P 500 anticipates a labor market cooling and produces a negative 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by >20,000 in a month AND UNRATE > 4% in the following two months
failure_condition: Over 5 such interaction-activated windows, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).
